story: On a humid, hazy Friday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is mounting a wired light harness and speaker bracket onto his golf cart, though the lights will stay off until Thanksgiving. Donna, determined as ever, is penciling a two-hour practice court slot for herself and Gary into the club calendar. Across the way, Hal stands on his porch with his binoculars, dutifully counting the flamingos he can spot in Donna's yard, while Rosa heads out onto Magnolia Loop with her own determined stride.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Mount the wired light harness and speaker bracket on the cart, lights left off until Thanksgiving
Donna (donna club calendar): Check the club schedule and pencil in a two-hour practice court slot for me and Gary
Hal (hal binoculars): Scan Donna's yard from the porch and count the flamingos visible from the street
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: Another morning, no one around, and I've got a cart to rig. The Architectural Review application is already filed, so the exterior mods are covered on paper, and Hal considers us square. Last tick I wired the light harness and bench-tested the speaker indoors and quiet. Now the cart itself is sitting right here. Holiday lighting isn't allowed until Thanksgiving under L-04, so I shouldn't hang anything visible from the street just yet, but I can do the mounting work and wiring in the garage and keep the cart in the driveway. No amplified sound issue at 8 AM since quiet hours ended at 7, but I'll keep volume low anyway. Time to put the harness on the cart and get useful.

parameters.content: Mount the wired light harness and speaker bracket on the cart, lights left off until Thanksgiving

donna.thought_process: I'm at Donna's House, but my memories say I just headed to the Rec Center with Gary and was checking the club calendar for a practice slot. Gary and I have the doubles ladder match coming up, and he's only agreed to a short session, so I want a court locked in before the morning gets away from us. No one is nearby, so the useful move is to use the calendar here and find a slot, keeping it within the 2-hour court limit under L-05.

parameters.content: Check the club schedule and pencil in a two-hour practice court slot for me and Gary

hal.thought_process: Gary's filed his paperwork, so the cart complaint is settled and I gave my word on a clean slate. The flamingos are the only item left. I logged yesterday's count at tick 162, and I've been staring at the same notebook for an hour. Procedure says I get a fresh count each morning before logging anything, so I'll take the binoculars and check the street-visible ornaments against the L-02 limit of three. It's 8 AM, no one's around, and I might as well do it right. Saturday at Rosa's is settled, so I can be fair about this, and a proper count is a fair count.

parameters.content: Scan Donna's yard from the porch and count the flamingos visible from the street

rosa.thought_process: It's Friday morning and the dinner is Saturday. The pork is marinating, the menu is set, the seating cards are out, and the shift schedule is already confirmed clear. The grocery list was finalized last tick, so the only thing left is actually buying the food. Nobody is nearby, so there's nobody to invite or remind. The one productive step is to head out toward Magnolia Loop and start the Friday errands, with the list in hand.

parameters.content: Heading out with the finalized list to run the Friday errands for Saturday's dinner: sides, drinks, backup dessert.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
